name: cloudflare-ddns-ec9ca53d-blind30-ots
instr:
# cloudflare-ddns-regen

This program watches which addresses a machine currently holds, keeps the published addresses for a list of names in step with them, and tells other services about it as it goes. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the machine, the settings written for it, or the services at the far end changed; the same runs that used to come out right now come out wrong, and what follows is what was noticed while using it, in the order the work was done.

Bringing it up and being told whether what was handed to it is acceptable goes wrong in several ways. Giving only the older of the two credential variables no longer yields a usable credential plus the one-time note that a newer name for it exists, and giving both, holding two different strings, no longer draws the refusal that they disagree; taking a credential out of a file, turning down a value surrounded by quotation marks, and catching a file that holds a whole VAR=value line rather than a bare value all still behave as written. Naming one alert destination directly while the file named by the matching setting holds a different one no longer draws the refusal that the two sources differ, and naming one directly while that file holds only blank and ignorable lines no longer draws the refusal that the file lists none; using only the file, only the direct value, or the same destination twice in either order still works, and complaints about several destinations folded onto on
